# Trump vows to hit Iran ‘hard’ despite US military war warning | Iran: the Latest news
## The Telegraph
6180000 subscribers
220 likes

### Description
2828 views
Posted: 1 Sep 2026
For the first time in over a month, fighting has erupted in the Strait of Hormuz after US forces struck Iranian sea mine-equipped rocket launchers on Larak Island. Iran retaliated by targeting US bases in Jordan, prompting Donald Trump to vow to hit Iran “hard”.  

On today's episode of Iran: The Latest, Venetia Rainey and Roland Oliphant unpack the details of the violence and why Trump has posted an AI video of an attack on Kharg Island. They also discuss why President Masoud Pezeshkian is calling for a return to the Memorandum of Understanding peace deal amid growing pressure on Iran’s economy from the US blockade.  

Plus, a leaked report shows top military commanders have warned Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth that the war is unsustainable, as US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll abruptly resigns amid growing chaos in the Pentagon.

# James Tunkey’s Post

![View profile for James Tunkey]()

On Iran, I seriously considered exiting a position tonight that Strait of Hormuz would stay closed through Jan 2027… asking if this week’s kinetic action by US, threats of new mining by IRGC, and the ongoing Oman negotiations just the prelude before peace.
I have kept my position open. Here is why.
The key variable in military regimes is whether the ruling officers retain a shared bargain: agreement over authority, spoils, and the rules by which disputes are settled. Regimes become vulnerable when that bargain breaks — when factions cease to coordinate, officers fear exclusion, or no accepted mechanism exists for resolving conflict within the elite.
The Aug 24 US OFAC toll alert and the IRGC’s toll architecture push the other way.
- Iran’s coercive elite has turned control of Hormuz into an organizational asset. Its now a revenue source, an enforcement role for the IRGC Navy, and a financing channel outside the civilian budget.
- The U.S. has treated the same system as a sanctionable institution.
